questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A well-acknowledged university and overall academic contribution to my studies/degree. Also being able to develop my german skills was a big plus, in addition to experiencing a new country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Munich is excellent, and the University is definitely of a higher academic level. However, I did find a lack of communication with the host University and the semester dates started much later than the ones at UCPH. This has forced me to postpone the following block in Denmark.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy. You receive an excess amount of informational e-mails upon arrival, but I would have appreciated receiving all of these at an "informational day for exchange students", and being given the opportunity to do so, earlier than 1 week before the semester starts.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was always a contact person, which was nice. But the informational days were not too fulfilling, and the study abroad department was sometimes very late in replying. I especially found it challenging with the course registration, as the system at TUM is more complex and old-school than most.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
In the future, it would be ideal to be offered an online meeting before arrival, where the course registration protocol is introduced and general support is given. 
Additionally, some TUM professors and/or course responsible were very late uploading course information, resulting in several of my planned courses not being offered as expected. This forced me to take some managerial courses outside of scope and campus to obtain my required credits in time. Hence, I did not satisfy my initial academic requirements for the study abroad.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not as easy as expected (and not cheap either). I was lucky enough to know someone who knew someone offering a room for rent in the center of Munich. I know some students chose to live outside Munich (such as Freising or Garching), which is doable, as the train connections work well. This might also save you some money. I did, however, prioritize location and therefore ended up paying around 750 € / month for a room in a shared apartment. There are also various groups on Facebook that could be worth checking out when starting your search.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Probably more expensive, but also a great chance to meet and engage with some locals.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, the course-registration system at TUM is not easy to navigate (and after talking with some professors at TUM, they might be upgrading it sometime soon...) In addition to this, an online introduction to the system before arrival would have been very valued.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online registration for courses opens shortly before arrival. However, bear in mind that not all of the courses are uploaded or visible at this point. Therefore you can "risk the chance" of getting a pre-approval for courses being given in prior years but not offered at this semester or year in particular (which happened to me). And note that there is a difference between courses & modules!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You receive a PDF with an "introduction to course registration," which is helpful. But additional online contact or service would have been excellent to smoothen the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: As stated above, I was forced to choose courses outside my faculty. This was due to: 1) my initial and pre-approved courses not being offered this year as expected, 2) an overlap of course schedule/teaching hours, and 3) limited spots.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Aim to have as many "non-limited" courses with you to make registration more flexible. And have a plan B, if you courses are not offered as expected or you are not offered a spot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Courses at my faculty (Life Science) met my expectations and were very satisfactory, as these were also similar to the structures offered at UCPH. However, the courses offered outside my faculty (e.g., School of Management) offered very different learning styles and not much support to the individual students (probably due to the size of the classes, which were typically > 100 students). Be aware of this.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was in general high and required you to do your homework and follow the lectures during the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some courses were similar (in-class teaching, group work, case study), and others were different from what I've had at SCIENCE back in Copenhagen (e.g., Seminars).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
As mentioned earlier, I was forced to choose courses outside my faculty to meet the required 30 ECTS points. Therefore I will list the courses separately.
School of Life Science: Consumer Behavior, Food Economics, and Food Design and Food Industry.
Outside: Key Issues in Businesses Today, Organizational Behavior, and Strategic and International Management.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you study food science or find the industry fascinating, I strongly recommend you to take the course in Freising by Mr. Pearson called 'Food Design and Food Industry.' Additionally, I enjoyed the course in Consumer Behavior which offers a broad insight into the psychological reasons for consuming products specifically related to the Food industry.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Købte en cykel til at have stående på stationen i Freising (Dette var super rart da der er 30-40 min gang fra stationen til Campus, dog ikke strengt nødvendigt da der går busser ofte). 

Fitness / trænings medlemsskab. Her købte jeg "ClassPass" som er en tysk app (findes også andre så som UrbanSports etc.). Dette giver dig adgang til en række af forskellige aktiviter om måneden rundet omkring i München (fitnesscentre, svømmehaller, yoga, sauna etc.) og kan bestemt anbefales, hvis du ønsker at prøve lidt forskelligt af mens du er her.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: "Cost of living" er generelt en smule billigere end I DK. Jeg sparede derfor penge på at handle ind (endda nogle gange billigere at smutte ned til den lokale og spise en Döner til 5€).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Brugte jeg ikke (købte selv andet medlemsskab).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: De har vidst en ordning som tilbyder diverse typer af træning rundet omkring München. Tror bestemt det er værd at kigge på, hvis du allerede nu har en drøm om at dyrke noget specifikt under dit ophold (havde jeg ikke).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Museer om søndagen til 1-2€!
Afprøv nogle forskellige klubber (jeg trænede fx med EBF, EisbachFit, som er en udendørs trænings community. Dette gjorde det nemt at møde lokale og lære byen at kende på en anden måde).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sørg for at tage ud af byen med tog. Dette kan f.eks. være en dagstur til Tegernsee eller Walchensee, som begge tilbyder 10/10 hikes, bavariske spisesteder og smukkeste natur!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and smiling :)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Germans can be a bit reserved at some points (though mostly the older generation, who also LOVE to speak German and not English..).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Younger German generations are most friendly and open - and love Danes! I enjoy how they, particularly, enjoy the "everyday pleasures" such as dining out and drinking beer during the week.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the course registration and have a Plan B.
Start looking for housing a good deal in advance (especially if you want something in Munich).
Pack your active gear - cause the city is surrounded by incredible nature and the ALPS!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: OBS on choosing courses in ENGLISH and not German (unless you want to of course :) )

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, culture, country, and surroundings.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it challenging. Maybe for some locals, the language barrier, but I also spoke a bit of German prior to arriving which helped.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO TO MUNICH IF YOU CAN :) The most unique and beautiful city I have ever experienced in Germany, and SO worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
